verdict_reason: My RED is resolved for the quantity that ships. `unembedding_eff_rank` is now the Roy-Vetterli effective rank of W_out ITSELF, and I confirmed end-to-end rather than by reading: running the task on gpt2 at defaults.yaml returns 685.9735952959319, bit-for-bit my independent uncentered erank of the same lm_head (685.9736), while the centered value on that matrix is 714.3684 (+4.14%). Against R&V Sec. 2.3's closed form for the 4x4 circulant with eigenvalues (1+|r|)^2, 1-r^2, 1-r^2, (1-|r|)^2 the uncentered path is exact -- 3.079201 vs closed-form 3.079201 at r = 0.5 (rel +0.0000%) and 1.487401 vs 1.487401 at r = 0.9 (rel -0.0000%) -- where the centered path returns 2.729839 (-11.35%) and 2.213602 (+48.82%), the error changing sign with the matrix, exactly as I reported. On real unembeddings the centering error runs 0.5% to 57.9% (pythia-70m 296.111 -> 467.526, +57.9%; pythia-160m 495.536 -> 710.149, +43.3%).
comparable_reason: unembedding_eff_rank is a width readout even uncentered. Over 18 models whose lm_head/tied-embedding I loaded directly (d_model 512..2048, vocab 32k..256k): Spearman +0.921 with d_model (p = 6.2e-8), Pearson r = +0.979; vs vocab_size only +0.143 and n_layers +0.128. erank/d_model sits at 0.94-0.97 for 14 of the 18 (pythia-410m 0.966, pythia-1b 0.966, Qwen3-1.7B 0.973, Llama-3.2-1B 0.965, TinyLlama 0.964, phi-1_5 0.942), so the number is essentially d_model times a near-constant. The uncentered form is at least slightly MORE informative than the centered one it replaced: erank/d spans 0.578-0.973 uncentered against 0.856-0.982 centered (Pearson with d_model +0.979 vs +0.995). No normalized twin is emitted.
normalized_variant: unembedding_eff_rank_scalenorm and unembedding_eff_rank_centered_scalenorm (both = the effective rank / d_model; NORMALIZERS in src/blme/normalization.py)
github_reason: Roy & Vetterli 2007 (EUSIPCO 2007, pp. 606-610) is a five-page signal-processing paper with no released code; the PDF contains only Definition 1, four properties and one closed-form example. Category purity and embedding alignment are BLME inventions with no upstream implementation, which task_metadata states accurately. There is nothing to cross-run, so the check is against the paper's own closed form (below).
paper_reason: R&V Sec. 2.3's 4x4 circulant closed form erank(A) = exp{2H((1+|rho|)/2, (1-|rho|)/2)}: the shipped uncentered path reproduces it to machine precision -- 3.079201435678 measured vs 3.079201435678 closed-form at rho = 0.5 and 1.487401275304 vs 1.487401275304 at rho = 0.9, relative error 0.0000% at both. Under the previous centered path the same anchors read 2.729839 (-11.35%) and 2.213602 (+48.82%).
confounds_reason: n = 18 directly loaded unembedding matrices: rho(d_model) = +0.921 (p = 6.2e-8), Pearson +0.979. The archived 25-model snapshot (which stores the old centered values) gives rho = +0.980. Matched-width models are nearly tied: at d = 2048, pythia-1b 1977.85, SmolLM2-1.7B 1955.88, Llama-3.2-1B 1976.15, TinyLlama 1974.12, phi-1_5 1928.81, Qwen3-1.7B 1993.63 -- a 3.3% spread across six different families. embedding_alignment_mean remains essentially a weight-tying indicator.
defects: CODE: `eff_rank_centered` is computed and never returned. The comment promises the centered variant is 'retained under a name that says what it is', but the return dict has no unembedding_eff_rank_centered key -- I ran the task and confirmed its absence. The consequence is a wasted second SVD of a (V, d) matrix on every run (50257x768 on gpt2, 256000x2048 on gemma-2b), which was the single slowest call in the library before the GPU move.

CODE: on the exception path `eff_rank` is set to NaN but `eff_rank_centered` is never bound; currently harmless only because the variable is unused, so wiring the key up without also fixing the except block will turn an SVD failure into a NameError.

No width-normalized twin exists. unembedding_eff_rank / d_model would be the obvious one; measured, it moves rho(d_model) from +0.921 to +0.501 -- better but not clean, because erank/d itself drifts with vocab/width (0.578 at pythia-70m to 0.973 at Qwen3-1.7B).

cross_model_comparable is emitted as False whenever any category token is found and True otherwise; it describes the purity field only, but reads as a statement about the whole task, and unembedding_eff_rank (rho +0.921 with d_model) is exactly the field it is not describing.

unembedding_purity_mean is tokenizer-dependent by construction (815 single-token category words on gpt2), which the comparability_note says -- but the count itself, unembedding_n_category_tokens, is emitted unprefixed and is a vocabulary proxy.
fix: Add "unembedding_eff_rank_centered": float(eff_rank_centered) to the return dict (and initialise it to NaN alongside eff_rank in the except branch), or delete the centered computation entirely -- as written it costs a full second SVD and produces nothing. Separately, emit unembedding_eff_rank_frac = eff_rank / d_model so the field is not a width readout in the feature matrix. NORMALIZED-VARIANT AXIS (measured 2026-09-04): the eff_rank/d_model twin suggested above is now registered as unembedding_eff_rank_scalenorm (and _centered_scalenorm) and both are RED. The mechanism is sound in principle -- effective rank IS proportional to d for a broad spectrum, measured erank/d = 0.99984 at d = 64 falling only to 0.99482 at d = 2048 for an iid Gaussian (50000, d) matrix -- but real unembeddings do not sit at a fixed fraction of the bound: over 27 freshly measured models erank goes as d^+1.146, so erank/d_model still carries rho(d_model) = +0.643 (p = 3e-04), down from +0.977 but nowhere near removed, and it turns a weak vocabulary association into a strong one (+0.418 -> +0.596, p = 1e-03). The centered twin fails differently: erank_centered/d_model spans only 0.9131-0.9822 (cv = 0.023) -- a near-constant, the failure mode that got chain_length_per_sample/n_layers and max_norm_layer/(L-1) deleted -- while still carrying rho(d_model) = +0.519 (p = 0.006) and rho(vocab) = +0.609 (p = 8e-04). Occupancy is not stable across the zoo either: erank/d runs 0.578 (pythia-70m) and 0.645 (pythia-160m) against 0.94-0.97 for most models, so the low end is set by two narrow models rather than by width itself. Remove both registrations.
fix_applied: R24: registered normalized twins for unembedding_eff_rank and _centered, divided by d_model -- an effective rank is bounded by d_model, and over 18 models the raw value has rho +0.921 with d_model (Pearson +0.979) against only +0.143 with vocab_size.
